replace.new:
[SET 30 Sep] On the way down to White Flower, after a wrong fork, a stranger on a rock above the path — Ari, a tengu in a man's guise (Cast › Ari) — flew them by the hand up the face of the mountain to an aerie shrine said to be **Kisshōten's retreat**. On the right day, it is said, Tengoku can be seen from it.

[SET 30 Sep] The shrine is not Rokugani: an archway that is not a torii but serves as one, unworked stone with ornaments added, an altar growing out of the rock, about four feet by two. Juri burned incense, improvising. Norikage offered a blessing that asked for nothing, and the tengu said: "Your children will be blessed." He unmasked in tears and his strife cleared.

[SET 30 Sep] They spent the night on the ledge (Scenes › Something crosses to the moon). At dawn the tengu flew them down over the treetops to a mile from White Flower.

[SOURCE] `writ-of-wilds-peoples.lore` — *Although one's role in society may be ever changing, a tengu aerie is run much like a monastery, with set schedules, rituals, and meditation at the heart of daily living.*

people.title: Ari, a tengu
people.text:
[SET 30 Sep] A tengu, known as Ari, who says he has no clan. His guise: a man of about forty sitting on a rock above a path, with a gnarled staff nearly straight and a large pack under a blanket worn like a cloak, his steps awkward. The pack is his wings, twelve or fifteen feet across. His hands are thin and wrinkled. He carries people through the air by the hand.

[SET 30 Sep] Norikage called him brother. He told Norikage that his children will be blessed, and, asked whether what he cannot understand troubles him: "I seek to understand what I may, but when things elude me, I make my peace with it, and I try again the following day."

[OPEN] Where his aerie is, and whether he is seen again.

append.text: [YOURS] **Kaito Juri and Togashi Norikage are the likely lovers**, and the likely parents of the children the tengu blessed.
